14899               	;
14900               	; #if NES
14901               	; 	' ----------------------------------------------------------------------
14902               	; 	' THE ATTRIBUTE TABLE -- the NES's only way of giving two parts of the
14903               	; 	' screen different colours.
14904               	; 	'
14905               	; 	' 64 bytes at $23C0. Each byte covers FOUR character rows and four
14906               	; 	' columns, split into four 2x2 quadrants of two bits each: bits 0-1 top
14907               	; 	' left, 2-3 top right, 4-5 bottom left, 6-7 bottom right.
14908               	; 	'
14909               	; 	' The picture sits three rows down for overscan, which lands the regions
14910               	; 	' on block boundaries almost by luck:
14911               	; 	'
14912               	; 	'   byte row 0   name rows 0-3    the HUD is row 3  -> bottom quads P1
14913               	; 	'   byte row 1   name rows 4-7    the sky, top half -> P2, bottom -> P3
14914               	; 	'   byte rows 2+ name rows 8-29   the store         -> P0
14915               	; 	'
14916               	; 	' $50 is "bottom two quadrants on palette 1"; $FA is "top two on palette
14917               	; 	' 2, bottom two on palette 3", which is what splits the sunset into a
14918               	; 	' blue band over a warm one. Written as bare literals because this is the
14919               	; 	' one place the bit layout is visible, and naming them would hide it.
14920               	; 	'
14921               	; 	' 64 VPOKEs is 192 bytes of PPU queue, and WRTVRM waits when the 64-byte
14922               	; 	' buffer fills, so this paces itself across three frames and cannot
14923               	; 	' overrun vblank the way a single big SCREEN blit can.
14924               	; 	' A MESSAGE BOX GOES WHITE ON DARK BLUE, and the caller says which four
14925               	; 	' bytes in #nav.
14926               	; 	'
14927               	; 	' The text's paper is index 1 and its ink index 3 (see the font upload);
14928               	; 	' over the store those are P0's green and gold -- the same green the box is
14929               	; 	' sitting on, which is what made the messages hard to read. P1 is the HUD's
14930               	; 	' palette, dark blue and white, so pointing the box's attribute bytes at it
14931               	; 	' gives a message the same treatment as the score line.
14932               	; 	'
14933               	; 	' FOUR BYTES AND NOT ONE MORE. An attribute byte covers four characters by
14934               	; 	' four, and the box is sized and placed to cover exactly four of them
14935               	; 	' (gentitle.py BOX_ROW/BOX_COL/BOX_W): byte columns 2..5, which is name
14936               	; 	' columns 8..23. Anything wider would recolour shop floor beside the box.
14937               	; 	'
14938               	; 	' THIS IS A ROUTINE BECAUSE IT WAS WRITTEN OUT TWICE AND MISSED A THIRD
14939               	; 	' TIME. GOT HIM! kept the store's colours while the other boxes changed,
14940               	; 	' and nothing failed -- it is a readable message in the wrong palette.
14941               	; 	' checkmsg.py now fails the build if a message box is drawn without one of
14942               	; 	' these beside it.
14943               	; 	'
14944               	; 	' Nothing puts them back, because nothing needs to: every path out of a
14945               	; 	' message box redraws the screen, and draw_screen calls nes_attr, which
14946               	; 	' rewrites all sixty-four.
14947               	; nes_boxatt:
14948               	; 	FOR nai = 0 TO 3
14949               	; 		VPOKE #nav,85
14950               	; 		#nav = #nav + 1
14951               	; 	NEXT nai
14952               	; 	RETURN
14953               	;
14954               	; nes_attr:
14955               	; 	#nav = 9152			' $23C0
14956               	; 	' $55, NOT $50 -- ALL FOUR QUADRANTS ON P1, not just the bottom two.
14957               	; 	'
14958               	; 	' $50 put the HUD's own row (name row 2) on P1 and left rows 0-1 on P0.
14959               	; 	' That was invisible while text sat on the backdrop, and stopped being so
14960               	; 	' the moment the font gained a PAPER: rows 0-1 are blank cells, and a blank
14961               	; 	' cell is all paper, so they came out in P0's index 1 -- the store's GREEN

15432               	;
15433               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
15434               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
15435               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
15436               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
15437               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
15438               	; 	'
15439               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
15440               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
15441               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
15442               	; 	'
15443               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
15444               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
15445               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
15446               	; 	'
15447               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
15448               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
15449               	; 	'
15450               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
15451               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
15452               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
15453               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
15454               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
15455               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
15456               	; 	'
15457               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
15458               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
15459               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
15460               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
15461               	; 	'
15462               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300

15583               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.

15587               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
15588               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
15589               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
15590               	; 	'
15591               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
15592               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
15593               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
15594               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
15595               	; 	' counting stops.
15596               	;
15597               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
15598               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
15599               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
15600               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
15601               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
15602               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
15603               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
15604               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
15605               	; 	'
15606               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
15607               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
15608               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).

15653               	; 	' THE CAST IS NOT TAKEN AWAY YET -- hide_all now runs AFTER the beat.
15654               	; 	'
15655               	; 	' It used to run here, so the moment the clock emptied, Harry and the
15656               	; 	' thing that had just hit him vanished and the sound played over an empty
15657               	; 	' store. The hit that ENDS a round is the worst case: `do_hit` sets tout
15658               	; 	' before the freeze starts and the main loop leaves on the very next pass,
15659               	; 	' so the hit sound gets one tick and everything is already gone.
15660               	; 	'
15661               	; 	' The pause drains the sound; leaving the actors up means it drains over
15662               	; 	' the picture that caused it. Nothing is moving -- the pause ticks sfx_tick
15663               	; 	' and nothing else -- so it is a held tableau, not a frozen game.
15664               	; 	' THE MESSAGE BOX, ON THE GAME SCREEN AND NOT INSTEAD OF IT.
15665               	; 	'
15666               	; 	' It used to CLS before GAME OVER, so the last thing the player saw was
15667               	; 	' the store being deleted and then two words on an empty field -- which
15668               	; 	' reads as the program ending rather than as the game ending. The store
15669               	; 	' stays; the message sits in the middle of it.
15670               	; 	'
15671               	; 	' THE BOX IS THE FONT'S OWN BACKGROUND. Every font character is black on
15672               	; 	' HUD_BG (dark blue), so a row of SPACES is a solid dark blue bar. A blank
15673               	; 	' row above and below the text is a frame for the price of two strings and
15674               	; 	' no new characters, and it reads against the store because nothing else on
15675               	; 	' the playfield is that colour.
15676               	; 	'
15677               	; 	' THIRTEEN WIDE, WHICH IS THE LONGEST MESSAGE PLUS ONE EITHER SIDE.
15678               	; 	' HE GOT AWAY and THE BIPLANE are both eleven. Every string below is padded
15679               	; 	' to exactly thirteen so the box has straight edges, and column 10 puts it
15680               	; 	' at columns 10-22 -- centre 16, the screen's.
15681               	; 	'
15682               	; 	' THE REASON IS ALWAYS ON THE SAME ROW, and that is what lets one layout
15683               	; 	' serve both cases. Losing a life draws three rows around it; losing the
15684               	; 	' last one draws two more ON TOP, so GAME OVER appears above the reason
15685               	; 	' rather than replacing it. Printing the reason at a different row for each
15686               	; 	' case would need `PRINT AT` with a variable, and every other PRINT in this
15687               	; 	' program uses a constant.
15688               	; 	#if NES
15689               	; 	' FLUSH THE PASS BEFORE DRAWING A BOX. PPUBUF accumulates for a whole loop
15690               	; 	' pass and is emptied by one NMI, so a message box -- sixty-four cells,
15691               	; 	' sixty-four single-byte descriptors -- was landing in the same vblank as
15692               	; 	' every radar poke and HUD digit the pass had made. The copy then ran past
15693               	; 	' the end of vblank and the tail was DISCARDED at the PPU: a box with
15694               	; 	' characters missing, and the cut moving from run to run, which is why it
15695               	; 	' read as intermittent corruption.
15696               	; 	'
15697               	; 	' One WAIT here empties the buffer; the box's own writes then self-pace,
15698               	; 	' because WRTVRM waits when PPUBUF fills. That is also why the TITLE never
15699               	; 	' needed this and must not have it: it is drawn at boot with nothing else
15700               	; 	' queued, and a WAIT per run made its twelve runs appear one frame at a
15701               	; 	' time -- a logo that visibly assembled itself.
15702               	; 	WAIT
15703               	; 	#endif

15953               	;
15954               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
15955               	; 	'
15956               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
15957               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
15958               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
15959               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
15960               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
15961               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
15962               	; 	'
15963               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
15964               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
15965               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
15966               	; 	'
15967               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
15968               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
15969               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
15970               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
15971               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
15972               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
15973               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
15974               	; 	'
15975               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
15976               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
15977               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
15978               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
15979               	; 	'
15980               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
15981               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
15982               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
15983               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
15984               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
15985               	; 	'
15986               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
15987               	; 	' did not finish.
15988               	; pause_beat:
15989               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

16351               	;
16352               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
16353               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
16354               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
16355               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
16356               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
16357               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
16358               	;
16359               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
16360               	; 	'
16361               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
16362               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
16363               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
16364               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
16365               	; 	'
16366               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
16367               	; 	'
16368               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
16369               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
16370               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
16371               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
16372               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
16373               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
16374               	; 	'
16375               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
16376               	; 	'
16377               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
16378               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
16379               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
16380               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
16381               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
16382               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
16383               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
16384               	; 	'
16385               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
16386               	; 	'
16387               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
16388               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
16389               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
16390               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
16391               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
16392               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
16393               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
16394               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
16395               	; 	'
16396               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
16397               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
16398               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
16399               	; 	'
16400               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
16401               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
16402               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
16403               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
16404               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
16405               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
16406               	; 	'
16407               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
16408               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
16409               	; 	'
16410               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
16411               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
16412               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
16413               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
16414               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
16415               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
16416               	; 	'
16417               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
16418               	; 	'
16419               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
16420               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
16421               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to

16424               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not

16624               	;
16625               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
16626               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
16627               	; 	'
16628               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
16629               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
16630               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
16631               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
16632               	; 	'
16633               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
16634               	; 	'
16635               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
16636               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
16637               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
16638               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
16639               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
16640               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
16641               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
16642               	; 	'
16643               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
16644               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
16645               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
16646               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
16647               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
16648               	; 	'
16649               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
16650               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
16651               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
16652               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
16653               	; 	#if TI994A
16654               	; 	BANK 2
16655      0168     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

17129               	; 	' AND THE TITLE'S DISPLAY LIST, for the same reason as the font: walked
17130               	; 	' once by title_draw, at boot and on a return to the title, and never
17131               	; 	' during play. title_draw selects bank 2 around its walk.
17132               	; 	'
17133               	; 	' ITS MESSAGE BOXES DID NOT COME WITH IT. They are the same format and
17134               	; 	' were in the same generated file, which is what made this worth doing
17135               	; 	' carefully: they are walked when a ROUND ENDS, mid-game, so on bank 2
17136               	; 	' they would have returned bytes from the wrong page at the moment a life
17137               	; 	' is lost -- and with no error at build or run time. gentitle.py now
17138               	; 	' writes them to title.bas below, which stays in bank 1.
17139               	; 	INCLUDE "titledl.bas"
17140               	; 	' ==================================================
17141               	; 	' THE TITLE SCREEN, AS A DISPLAY LIST
17142               	; 	' Generated by assets/gentitle.py -- do not edit here.
17143               	; 	'
17144               	; 	' row, col, length, then `length` bytes; 255 ends.
17145               	; 	' Walked by title_draw only.
17146               	; 	'
17147               	; 	' LIVES IN BANK 2, with the fonts, because it is read ONCE
17148               	; 	' -- at boot and on a return to the title. title_draw
17149               	; 	' selects bank 2 around its walk and restores bank 1.
17150               	; 	' The message boxes in title.bas are the same format and
17151               	; 	' CANNOT come with it: they are read when a round ends.
17152               	; 	' ==================================================
17153               	;

17385               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
17386               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
17387               	; 	'
17388               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
17389               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
17390               	; 	' being small sprites.
17391               	; 	'
17392               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
17393               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
17394               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
17395               	; 	'
17396               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
17397               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
17398               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
17399               	;
17400               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/two merged run bodies/two FREE slots/duck hat/face/body, then the same LEFT (+36). The run bodies carry tunic AND legs, so a frame is one sprite, and standing is run frame 1. Patterns 0..68
17401               cvb_SPR_KELLY

18641               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
18642               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
18643               	; 	'
18644               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
18645               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
18646               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
18647               	; 	'
18648               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
18649               	; 	' blit is
18650               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
18651               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
18652               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
18653               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
18654               	; 	'
18655               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
18656               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
18657               	; 	'
18658               	; 	' template ids:
18659               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
18660               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
18661               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
18662               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
18663               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
18664               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
18665               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
18666               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
18667               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
18668               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
18669               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
18670               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
18671               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
18672               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
18673               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
18674               	;
18675               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes
18676               cvb_STOR_TPL

19292               	; 	' THE SKYLINE'S LAST BAND WITHOUT ITS YELLOW, high nibble ink, low nibble
19293               	; 	' paper, one byte a scan line -- the same shape genart emits into
19294               	; 	' store_col. SKY2 is white-on-9 throughout instead of turning to paper 10
19295               	; 	' at row 4; BLDGL holds its blue one row longer and then meets its own
19296               	; 	' grey wall. Both are the generated bytes with 10 replaced by 9 and
19297               	; 	' nothing else changed. See setup_rest.
19298               	; #if NES
19299               	; nes_sky2c:

19303               	; #endif
19304               	;
19305               	; 	' THE IN-GAME FONT'S COLOUR, one byte a scan line and eight a character for
19306               	; 	' all 59 of them. $B4 is light yellow on dark blue -- ink index 3, paper index 1 --
19307               	; 	' and which colours those are is then the attribute table's business, per
19308               	; 	' region: dark blue behind the HUD, the store's green behind a message box.
19309               	; 	'
19310               	; 	' 472 bytes of one repeated value. That reads like waste and is the cheap
19311               	; 	' option: ROM is three budgets here and this is not the scarce one, while
19312               	; 	' the alternative is a second font (impossible -- only eleven free codes)
19313               	; 	' or a new uploader parameter (no RAM -- two bytes left).
